content: When the Master governs, the people are hardly aware that he exists. When his work is done, his aim fulfilled, they will say: 'We did it ourselves.'
author: Lao Tzu
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Lao Tzu understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
